query: Consider the following context: Melting properties are critical for designing novel materials, especially for discovering high-performance, high-melting refractory materials. Experimental measurements of these properties are extremely challenging due to their high melting temperatures. Complementary theoretical predictions are, therefore, indispensable. One of the most accurate approaches for this purpose is the ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT). However, it generally involves expensive thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamic simulations. The high computational cost makes high-throughput calculations infeasible. In that context, which method can be used for calculate its melting properties, including the melting temperature, entropy and enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The melting properties of a refractory material can be accurately calculated using the ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT) with a machine learning-based interpolation scheme to reduce computational costs.
generation.material_initial_state: Solid state at standard temperature and pressure
generation.intervention: Ab initio free-energy calculations with machine learning-based interpolation
generation.conditions: Density functional theory (DFT) framework, machine learning-based interpolation scheme
generation.mechanism: Quantum mechanical calculations of free energy as a function of temperature and pressure
generation.predicted_outcome: Melting temperature within 10% of experimental value, entropy and enthalpy of fusion within 5% of experimental value, volume change at melting point within 2% of experimental value
generation.boundary: Refractory materials with high melting temperatures (>2000 K)
generation.uncertainty: Machine learning model accuracy, choice of exchange-correlation functional in DFT, convergence of thermodynamic integration

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of calculated melting properties with experimental measurements for a set of refractory materials
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the calculated melting temperature deviates by more than 15% from the experimental value for more than 50% of the tested materials, the hypothesis is falsified.
